# India smartphone prices jump 16% in first half of 2026; market seen shrinking double digits

SECTIONS

India smartphone prices jump 16% in first half of 2026; market seen shrinking double digits

ET OnlineLast Updated: Sep 29, 2026, 07:45:00 PM IST

Synopsis

Average smartphone selling prices in India rose by 16% year-over-year in the first half of 2026. OnePlus, however, managed to keep its price increase to just 8%, distinguishing itself from competitors. Entry-level devices saw an average price increase of 32%, resulting in a significant 65% drop in shipments. Meanwhile, premium smartphones priced above Rs 20,000 continued to grow, benefiting from trade-in programs.

India’s average mobile phone prices rose 16% as higher memory costs and a weaker rupee made imported components more expensive, Counterpoint Research said.

Average smartphone selling prices in India climbed 16% year-over-year in the first half of 2026, driven by a sharp rise in memory component costs and a depreciating rupee, according to market research firm Counterpoint Research.  
  
The surge pushed the country's average smartphone selling price to a record USD 318 in the second quarter of 2026. The broader smartphone market is now projected to contract by double digits, though Chinese brand OnePlus remains a notable exception due to more modest price adjustments.  
  
"Smartphone prices in India rose 16 per cent on average in the first half of 2026, but OnePlus kept its own increase to 8 per cent. The hikes came as memory costs climbed, pushing India's average smartphone selling price to a record USD 318 in the second quarter of 2026," the research firm said.  
  
  
  
Entry-level devices under Rs 10,000 experienced the most dramatic price increases—averaging roughly 32%—as memory makes up a larger percentage of the bill of materials for lower-cost devices. As a result, shipments in the sub-Rs 10,000 segment plunged 65% year-over-year in H1 2026. The mid-tier Rs 10,000–Rs 15,000 price band, long a dominant volume driver in India, also declined by 20%.  

### Live Events

  
In contrast, the premium tier held up far better. Smartphones priced above Rs 20,000 continued to grow, insulated by higher initial launch pricing, trade-in programs, and widespread access to no-cost EMI options that offset upfront price sensitivity.  
  
"AI data centres have been soaking up DRAM and NAND supply, and a weaker rupee has made imported components more expensive, leaving most brands with little choice but to raise prices through the first half of the year," the research firm said.  
  
Although nearly 99% of mobile phones sold in India are assembled locally, manufacturers remain heavily reliant on imported parts, exposing them to currency fluctuations and global component shortages.  
  
While most brands chose to pass soaring costs directly to consumers, OnePlus managed to keep its average price hike to just 8%.  
  
"Its (OnePlus biggest single price increase was 12 per cent, compared with 113 per cent for the rest of the industry, so the gap held not just on average but at the extremes as well. The lower hikes also did not hurt growth," the firm said.  
  
  
  
The strategy helped OnePlus become the fastest-growing brand among the top five on online channels in the above-Rs 20,000 price bracket during Q2 2026.  
  
"OnePlus shipments are forecast to grow 5 per cent YoY in the quarter, while the overall market is expected to shrink by double digits," the research firm said.  
  
The company avoided aggressive price increases by procuring and securing component stock earlier in the year, locking in memory rates before supply shortages intensified.  
  
"In a cost shock scenario like this, brands usually have to pick between two choices – hold prices and give up margin, or protect margin and give up volume. OnePlus's H1 numbers suggest it managed to avoid this, mostly because it secured components early and has a portfolio broad enough to spread the pressure instead of loading it onto one price band," Counterpoint Research, Research Director, Tarun Pathak said.  
  
The pricing pressure on hardware makers is unlikely to abate anytime soon. Counterpoint estimates that memory costs will remain elevated through at least 2028, with currency pressures continuing to weigh heavily on local assembly margins.

So, why are phones getting expensive? The answer isn't just one thing. Rising component costs, AI-powered hardware, import expenses, currency fluctuations, and higher manufacturing costs are all contributing to the mobile price hike in India. Understanding these factors can help you decide whether it's the right time to upgrade and buy a smartphone now or wait for a better deal.

## Why Are Smartphones Getting More Expensive?

If you've been wondering why mobile phone prices are increasing, it comes down to how smartphones are made.

* Every smartphone is built using hundreds of components, including processors, displays, memory chips, camera sensors, batteries, and connectivity hardware.

* Features like 5G connectivity, AI-powered tools, larger batteries, fast charging, high-refresh-rate displays, and advanced cameras are becoming standard.

Together, these factors explain why smartphone prices are increasing in India.

## What's Driving the Smartphone Price Hike?

Several factors are contributing to the smartphone price hike India is witnessing today.

### AI is Increasing Component Costs

Artificial intelligence has created a huge demand for advanced processors and memory chips. Smartphone brands are also adding AI-powered features such as image editing, real-time translation, and smart assistants, which require more powerful hardware.

As demand for these components grows, manufacturers may have to pay more, leading to higher smartphone prices.

### Imported Components Are Costlier

Although many smartphones are assembled in India, several important parts are still imported. If the rupee weakens or import costs increase, manufacturers may have to spend more on processors, displays, memory chips, and camera sensors.

These additional costs often contribute to the mobile price hike in India.

### Supply Chain Challenges

Smartphones rely on a global supply chain. Delays in manufacturing, shipping disruptions, or shortages of key components can increase production costs and affect product availability, which may also influence retail prices.

## Should You Buy a Smartphone Now?

If your current phone is slow, has poor battery life, no longer receives software updates, or doesn't meet your daily needs, it may be a good time to upgrade. While the smartphone price hike may continue due to rising production costs, waiting doesn't always guarantee lower prices.
